what: Sol start_percent on the t2v pick (h3_text_to_video_pdd8_flashgen_finish), 0.2 as shipped against 0.0, on five 345-frame bank scenes chosen to differ (crowd and music, fast swordplay, nature with voiceover, dialogue close-ups, 2D cartoon). Owner-approved 2026-10-01 (review1001, item 1).
why: start_percent 0.2 puts sigma 1.0 and 0.988 outside Sol's window (the server log prints the window as [0, 0.9796]), so 2 of the finish's 8 evaluations run dense. On 2026-10-01 the ref2va finish's two dense steps ran about 65 s each against about 39 s per Sol step (server log timestamps against bench/results/2026-10-01_mutant_parity_flashgen_i2v_r2v_finish.jsonl), and docs/attention/sol_attn.md says the setting was never measured. Removing dense warm-up moves the sample into another basin, so a distance metric cannot score it (docs/state/next_steps.md, the start_percent note); the owner judges blind pairs. Upstream gives no lower default to adopt: core's BlockSparseAttention also defaults to 0.2.

seeds.note: held: one seed per scene, the pair differs only in start_percent

blind: blind_batch.py --pairs sp020,sp000 over the rows (see docs/method/eval_comparison.md section 3)
order: per scene, 0.2 then 0.0, so the second arm reuses the scene's text encode; the two arms share no sampler cache (Sol's window differs).
next: If 0.0 loses, 0.1 is the next arm: it leaves only sigma 1.0 dense (percent_to_sigma at shift 12 puts the edge near 0.991).
